# Deep Research Intelligence Packet

## Cycle metadata

- Packet ID: `dr-20260930-1008-berry-ai-validation`
- Research system: `Codex web research`
- Started at: `2026-09-30 10:08 CDT`
- Completed at: `2026-09-30 10:13 CDT`
- Research scope: Validate four first-party Berry AI customer, case-study, and product-positioning pages for named restaurant relationships, rollout scope, products, and evidence limitations.
- Queue item or vendor: `competitor:berry-ai`
- Methodology: First-party customer-story, rollout-announcement, operator-story, and segment-page validation with vendor-claim labeling and franchisee-versus-enterprise boundaries preserved.

## Executive result

- Pages reviewed: 4
- Candidate pages validated: 4
- Brand-vendor-product observations added or revised: 4
- Company/competitor profile observations added or revised: 4
- Conflicts found: 4
- Material takeaway: Berry AI has first-party evidence for a brand-wide Culver's Vision AI rollout announced across 1,000-plus locations, a four-store Georgia Zaxby's franchisee deployment of its Drive-Thru Timer, a selected-location Wenspok Companies deployment of camera-based timers, and an unnamed Little Caesars franchisee testimonial. The sources support drive-thru and counter vision analytics, not POS or payment processing. Scope and outcome claims remain vendor-authored, and the Little Caesars and Wenspok pages do not establish estate-wide deployments.

## Evidence observations

### Observation 1

- Brand: Culver's
- Vendor: Berry AI
- Product or category: Vision AI for service execution, vehicle flow, throughput, and performance measurement across drive-thru, dine-in, and pickup
- Relationship indication: customer
- Deployment scope: enterprise
- Evidence type: press release / vendor announcement
- Confidence: 95%
- Confidence rationale: Berry AI announces a brand-wide deployment across all 1,000-plus Culver's locations and includes a direct statement attributed to Culver's COO; the page remains vendor-controlled and does not independently verify completion timing or exact active-location count.
- Source title: What a 1,000-Location Vision AI Rollout Signals for QSR
- Source URL: https://www.berry-ai.com/blog/what-a-1-000-location-vision-ai-rollout-signals-for-qsr/
- Publisher or source owner: Berry AI
- Published date, if known: 2026-05-08
- Accessed date: 2026-09-30
- Exact supporting excerpt or faithful factual note: Berry AI says its brand-wide Culver's partnership deploys the Vision AI platform across all 1,000-plus locations and measures service execution, vehicle flow, throughput, and performance across drive-thru, dine-in, and pickup.
- Product-specific evidence: The platform is described as fitting existing workflows and POS ecosystems without replacing them and as delivering real-time operational visibility to restaurant teams and leadership.
- Conflicting or limiting evidence: The source is a Berry AI announcement. It does not disclose rollout milestones, contract terms, integrations, store-level activation dates, or customer-controlled outcome measurements. "All 1,000+" is announced scope and should not be treated as independently audited completion.
- Recommended follow-up: Confirm current active-location count, rollout completion, and named POS integrations from Culver's or another customer-controlled source.

### Observation 2

- Brand: Zaxby's franchisee (anonymous)
- Vendor: Berry AI
- Product or category: Berry AI Drive-Thru Timer, kitchen monitor, and cloud dashboard
- Relationship indication: customer
- Deployment scope: franchisee
- Evidence type: case study
- Confidence: 95%
- Confidence rationale: Berry AI's case study identifies the brand, four-store Georgia franchisee scope, product, replacement technology, surfaces, and a 90-day rollout; the operator identity is withheld and all performance results are vendor-published.
- Source title: Zaxby's Operator Reverses a 10% Slide by Installing Berry AI Drive-Thru Timer in Georgia
- Source URL: https://www.berry-ai.com/case-studies/zaxby-s-operator-reverses-a-10-slide-by-installing-berry-ai-drive-thru-timer-in-georgia/
- Publisher or source owner: Berry AI
- Published date, if known: 2025-06-20
- Accessed date: 2026-09-30
- Exact supporting excerpt or faithful factual note: The case study identifies an anonymous Zaxby's franchisee operating four Georgia locations and says Berry AI's camera timer, kitchen monitor, and cloud dashboard replaced an aging loop-detector timer over a 90-day, four-store rollout.
- Product-specific evidence: Queue, speaker, and window timing; pre-menu queue and drive-off visibility; staffing and food-preparation adjustments; kitchen monitor; and cloud dashboard are explicit.
- Conflicting or limiting evidence: The page does not name the franchisee or establish a corporate Zaxby's deployment. Reported sales-gap and service-time improvements are vendor-authored and not independently audited.
- Recommended follow-up: Identify the franchise operator and confirm current four-store status and any expansion through operator-controlled materials.

### Observation 3

- Brand: Wenspok Companies
- Vendor: Berry AI
- Product or category: Camera-based drive-thru timers with pre-menu queue, drive-off, real-time operational, and food-preparation signals
- Relationship indication: customer
- Deployment scope: pilot
- Evidence type: customer story
- Confidence: 85%
- Confidence rationale: Berry AI names Wenspok Companies and describes selected-location testing and a commitment to expand, but does not disclose brands, locations, store count, product version, or evidence that the promised expansion completed.
- Source title: How Wenspok Companies Transformed Customer Service with Berry's Camera-Based Timers
- Source URL: https://www.berry-ai.com/blog/how-wenspok-companies-transformed-customer-service-with-berry-s-camera-based-timers/
- Publisher or source owner: Berry AI
- Published date, if known: 2023-09-01
- Accessed date: 2026-09-30
- Exact supporting excerpt or faithful factual note: Berry AI says Wenspok tested its camera-based timers in selected locations, used pre-menu queue and drive-off information for operating decisions and food preparation, and intended to expand to more locations.
- Product-specific evidence: Above-ground camera timing, real-time queue and drive-off data, historical car-count comparisons, and operational adjustments are described.
- Conflicting or limiting evidence: The source does not name the restaurant brands or locations, quantify the pilot, or confirm that expansion occurred. The reported 14.9% service-speed improvement is vendor-authored.
- Recommended follow-up: Resolve Wenspok's deployed brands and locations and verify whether the expansion moved beyond the pilot.

### Observation 4

- Brand: Little Caesars franchisee (unnamed)
- Vendor: Berry AI
- Product or category: AI-based timer for counter and drive-thru visibility
- Relationship indication: customer
- Deployment scope: franchisee
- Evidence type: testimonial
- Confidence: 70%
- Confidence rationale: Berry AI's current pizza segment page attributes a product-selection testimonial to a Little Caesars franchisee, but gives no operator identity, location count, date, rollout status, or specific Berry AI configuration.
- Source title: Pizza | Berry AI
- Source URL: https://www.berry-ai.com/customers/pizza/
- Publisher or source owner: Berry AI
- Published date, if known: Undated
- Accessed date: 2026-09-30
- Exact supporting excerpt or faithful factual note: The page attributes to "Jim, Little Caesars Franchisee" a statement that the franchisee chose Berry's AI-based timer to improve customer experience.
- Product-specific evidence: The page positions Berry AI for counter and drive-thru arrival-to-handoff measurement, queue and walk-out visibility, throughput, prep timing, staffing, and cross-location service-time comparison.
- Conflicting or limiting evidence: The testimonial does not identify the legal operator, stores, current deployment status, product configuration, or measured outcome. Segment-page ROI figures are estimates and are not Little Caesars results.
- Recommended follow-up: Identify the franchise group and verify installed-store count and exact product through a customer-controlled or location-level source.

## Company / competitor profile observations

### Company profile observation 1

- Target: `competitor:berry-ai`
- Field: key_customers
- Value or observation: Berry AI announced a brand-wide Culver's Vision AI deployment across 1,000-plus locations covering service execution, vehicle flow, throughput, and performance measurement across drive-thru, dine-in, and pickup.
- Confidence: 95%
- Confidence rationale: The named announcement includes a statement attributed to Culver's COO and explicit enterprise scope, but deployment completion and active-store count are not independently audited.
- Source title: What a 1,000-Location Vision AI Rollout Signals for QSR
- Source URL: https://www.berry-ai.com/blog/what-a-1-000-location-vision-ai-rollout-signals-for-qsr/
- Publisher or source owner: Berry AI
- Published date, if known: 2026-05-08
- Accessed date: 2026-09-30
- Exact supporting excerpt or faithful factual note: Berry AI describes the partnership as brand-wide and says the platform is being deployed across all 1,000-plus Culver's locations.
- Conflicting or limiting evidence: Treat 1,000-plus as announced enterprise scope, not an independently verified count of active installations.

### Company profile observation 2

- Target: `competitor:berry-ai`
- Field: key_customers
- Value or observation: An anonymous four-store Georgia Zaxby's franchisee deployed Berry AI Drive-Thru Timer with kitchen-monitor and cloud-dashboard surfaces over 90 days.
- Confidence: 95%
- Confidence rationale: The vendor case study provides unusually specific franchisee, region, store-count, product, and rollout details, but withholds the operator identity.
- Source title: Zaxby's Operator Reverses a 10% Slide by Installing Berry AI Drive-Thru Timer in Georgia
- Source URL: https://www.berry-ai.com/case-studies/zaxby-s-operator-reverses-a-10-slide-by-installing-berry-ai-drive-thru-timer-in-georgia/
- Publisher or source owner: Berry AI
- Published date, if known: 2025-06-20
- Accessed date: 2026-09-30
- Exact supporting excerpt or faithful factual note: The case study's customer summary lists Zaxby's franchise, four Georgia locations, Drive-Thru Timer, a 90-day rollout, kitchen monitor, and cloud dashboard.
- Conflicting or limiting evidence: This is franchisee scope, not corporate or systemwide Zaxby's adoption, and the operator remains unnamed.

### Company profile observation 3

- Target: `competitor:berry-ai`
- Field: key_customers
- Value or observation: Berry AI reports selected-location use of camera-based drive-thru timers by Wenspok Companies, with real-time pre-menu queue and drive-off signals and a stated intent to expand.
- Confidence: 85%
- Confidence rationale: Wenspok is named and the operational use is detailed, but the page does not identify brands, locations, store count, or completed expansion.
- Source title: How Wenspok Companies Transformed Customer Service with Berry's Camera-Based Timers
- Source URL: https://www.berry-ai.com/blog/how-wenspok-companies-transformed-customer-service-with-berry-s-camera-based-timers/
- Publisher or source owner: Berry AI
- Published date, if known: 2023-09-01
- Accessed date: 2026-09-30
- Exact supporting excerpt or faithful factual note: Berry AI says Wenspok began testing camera-based timers in selected locations and committed to expand after the test.
- Conflicting or limiting evidence: The page does not prove that expansion occurred and does not name the deployed restaurant brands.

### Company profile observation 4

- Target: `competitor:berry-ai`
- Field: key_customers
- Value or observation: Berry AI's pizza customer page attributes selection of its AI-based timer to an unnamed Little Caesars franchisee.
- Confidence: 70%
- Confidence rationale: This is a direct first-party testimonial with a named restaurant brand but an unidentified operator and no deployment detail.
- Source title: Pizza | Berry AI
- Source URL: https://www.berry-ai.com/customers/pizza/
- Publisher or source owner: Berry AI
- Published date, if known: Undated
- Accessed date: 2026-09-30
- Exact supporting excerpt or faithful factual note: The page attributes the timer-selection statement to "Jim, Little Caesars Franchisee."
- Conflicting or limiting evidence: No legal operator, location, store count, implementation date, product configuration, or outcome is disclosed.

## Negative findings

- Candidate or claim: The reviewed named relationships establish Berry AI as a POS, ordering, or payment-processing system of record.
- Pages checked: Four first-party Culver's, Zaxby's, Wenspok, and pizza customer pages.
- Result: The evidence supports vision-based timing, queue, throughput, service-execution, counter, and operational analytics. Culver's is expressly described as fitting existing POS ecosystems; no page establishes transaction processing or POS ownership.

- Candidate or claim: Wenspok or Little Caesars has an estate-wide Berry AI deployment.
- Pages checked: Wenspok customer story and Berry AI pizza customer page.
- Result: Wenspok is described as selected-location testing with future expansion intent; the Little Caesars evidence is an unnamed franchisee testimonial without store count. Neither supports systemwide adoption.

| https://www.berry-ai.com/case-studies/zaxby-s-operator-reverses-a-10-slide-by-installing-berry-ai-drive-thru-timer-in-georgia/ | Case study | 2026-09-30 | 2, profile 2 | Four-store anonymous Georgia franchisee deployment; outcomes vendor-reported. |
| https://www.berry-ai.com/blog/how-wenspok-companies-transformed-customer-service-with-berry-s-camera-based-timers/ | Customer story | 2026-09-30 | 3, profile 3 | Selected-location Wenspok test; brands, locations, and completed expansion unresolved. |
| https://www.berry-ai.com/customers/pizza/ | Segment customer page / testimonial | 2026-09-30 | 4, profile 4 | Unnamed Little Caesars franchisee selection; no store count or outcome. |

## Research notes and inferences

- Inference: Berry AI overlaps Genius primarily in restaurant operational intelligence around the drive-thru, counter, queue, service execution, and above-store visibility, rather than as a transaction-system POS or payments platform.
- Inference: Culver's is the strongest enterprise-scale signal in this batch; Zaxby's, Wenspok, and Little Caesars require careful operator-level scope labels.
- Review instruction: Preserve all outcome figures as vendor-reported, keep announced rollout scope distinct from independently verified active deployment, and do not promote unnamed franchisee or selected-location evidence into systemwide brand adoption.
